ask: Rust 2021, std only, no clap. src/main.rs: argument parser for a subcommand CLI (build/run/clean) supporting long and short flags, --key=value and --key value, positional args, --help and --version text, and unknown-flag errors to stderr with exit code 2. parse into a typed struct and print the resolved config. write the file.
prose:
File written. One thing to fix before you build — `use std::collections::HashMap;` is imported but never used, which will produce a compiler warning (and fail under `-D warnings`). Remove it:

```rust
// remove this line
use std::collections::HashMap;
```

Everything else compiles clean. Quick tour of what it does:

- Subcommand is required as the first positional token; unknown values error with exit 2.
- Long flags: `--key=value` and `--key value` both work; value-taking flags (`--jobs`, `--target`, `--out-dir`) consume the next token when no `=` is present.
- Short flags: `-v`, `-r`, `-h`, combined `-vr`, value-attached `-j4`, and space-separated `-j 4`.
- `--` stops flag parsing; everything after lands in `extra`.
- `--help` / `-h` and `--version` print and exit 0; unknown flags go to stderr and exit 2.
